prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1418; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a red light in the left lane of a city street in Pasadena, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was traveling behind it. Driver 2 stated that he was unable to stop in time. Driver 1 reported neck pain and was assisted by emergency medical personnel at the scene, where a Passenger seated in the front right position was also present and confirmed the sequence of events. Responding officers and nearby residents confirmed that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle at the time of impact, though no independent witnesses to the collision itself were located. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear bumper, trunk lid and tail lamp assembly, which is largely consistent with the reported impact. A few older scratches were also noted on the rear panel, and these may predate this incident. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy involved. Whether the reported neck injury resulted from this collision has not yet been determined and will require further medical review.
